Ruby's `irb` (Interactive Ruby) has syntax highlighting since Ruby 3.x. It uses a numbered prompt with `*` for continuation lines:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    shell: irb
    shell-args: ["--noautocomplete"]
    prompt: "irb"
    prompt-regex: "`irb\\(main\\):\\d+>\\s*$`"
    ps2-regex: "`irb\\(main\\):\\d+[*|]\\s*$`"
    disable-auto-indent: true
```

The `disable-auto-indent` option counteracts irb's automatic indentation of continuation lines.

## Basic Usage

```{term}
puts "Hello from Ruby #{RUBY_VERSION}"
```

## Expressions

```{term}
(1..10).sum
"hello".chars.map(&:upcase).join
```

## Arrays and Hashes

```{term}
squares = (1..5).map { |x| x ** 2 }
squares
data = {name: "quarto-term", language: "Ruby", version: RUBY_VERSION}
data.each { |k, v| puts "  #{k}: #{v}" }
```

## Methods

```{term}
def fibonacci(n)
  a, b = 0, 1
  n.times { a, b = b, a + b }
  a
end
(0...10).map { |i| fibonacci(i) }
```

## Blocks and Iterators

```{term}
%w[apple banana cherry].each_with_index do |fruit, i|
  puts "#{i + 1}. #{fruit}"
end
```
